sec1.titulo: An explanation that is easy to follow
abertura: When you explain a problem at work, the other person needs to follow your ideas.
Three of these sentences are true. Mark the three.

itens.t: It says why something happened.
itens.porque: Without the reason, the other person has to ask, or guess.

itens.t: It uses long and difficult words.
itens.porque: Simple words are easier to follow, especially in a meeting.

itens.t: It says what happened next, or what happens next.
itens.porque: People want to know what the situation is now, and what the plan is.

itens.t: It gives only the final result.
itens.porque: The result alone often brings the question: why?

itens.t: It connects the ideas instead of listing them.
itens.porque: A list of short facts leaves the other person to find the connection.

itens.t: It is better when it is very long.
itens.porque: A clear explanation can be short. Length does not make it clearer.

sec1.pt: Quando você explica um problema no trabalho, a outra pessoa precisa acompanhar as suas ideias. Marque as três frases verdadeiras.

sec2.pt: Escolha o sentido que cada expressão tem quando se fala de um problema no trabalho. Você pode usar essas palavras na aula.

sec3.titulo: A message about a video call

doc.titulo: From: Ana · To: The sales team
doc.texto: Hi team, the video call with the client started twenty minutes late because the link did not work. We sent a new link, so the call started at 10:20. The client liked the new plan, but they want a lower price. When I get the numbers from finance, I will send a new offer. Ana

abertura: Read the message. Three of these sentences are true. Mark the three.

itens.t: The call started late.
itens.porque: “started twenty minutes late”.

itens.t: The client did not like the new plan.
itens.porque: “The client liked the new plan.” The problem is the price.

itens.t: A new link solved the problem.
itens.porque: “We sent a new link, so the call started at 10:20.”

itens.t: Ana already sent a new offer.
itens.porque: She will send it later, after she gets the numbers from finance.

itens.t: Ana needs information from finance.
itens.porque: “When I get the numbers from finance, I will send a new offer.”

itens.t: The client wants a higher price.
itens.porque: The client wants a lower price.

sec3.pt: Leia a mensagem e marque as três frases verdadeiras sobre ela.

abertura: Look at Ana’s message again, in activity 3. What does each part of the sentence tell you?

itens.t: … because the link did not work.
itens.porque: It says why the call started late.

itens.t: … so the call started at 10:20.
itens.porque: It says what happened after the new link.

itens.t: … but they want a lower price.
itens.porque: The first part is good news. This part is not.

itens.t: … because the client was traveling.
itens.porque: It says why something happened.

itens.t: … so we moved the meeting to Friday.
itens.porque: It says what the team did after the first fact.

itens.t: … but the room was not free.
itens.porque: It changes the direction of the sentence.

sec4.pt: Olhe de novo a mensagem da Ana, na atividade 3. Diga o que cada parte da frase traz: um motivo, um resultado ou algo diferente do que veio antes.

abertura: Complete the notes about the words in Ana’s message.

itens.t: After because, you usually find
After so, you usually find
After but, you usually find

sec5.pt: Complete as anotações sobre as palavras da mensagem da Ana.

abertura: Write short notes about a problem at work.

callout.texto:
What happened? Why was it a problem? What did you or your team do?

Write notes, not full sentences. You can use your notes in your lesson.

sec6.pt:
Escreva anotações curtas sobre um problema no trabalho.

O que aconteceu? Por que foi um problema? O que você ou a sua equipe fizeram? Escreva anotações, não frases completas. Você pode usar as suas anotações na aula.

itens.t: The laptops arrived on Wednesday at five, so Nora started the installation that evening.
itens.porque: Nora started that evening because the laptops arrived. So brings what happened after.

itens.t: The installation took longer than we expected because two laptops had a problem with the password.
itens.porque: The password problem explains why it took longer.

itens.t: Nora fixed them on Thursday morning, but one laptop is still not working.
itens.porque: The first part is good news. After but comes the part that is still a problem.

itens.t: I will ask the supplier for a new one when they call me today.
itens.porque: When they call me says the moment Ryan will ask.

itens.t: The sales team has nineteen laptops now, so they can start using the new system this afternoon.
itens.porque: Having nineteen laptops makes it possible to start. So brings the result again.

itens.t: The meeting started late because the room was not free.
itens.porque: A new sentence with the same job: the room explains why the meeting started late.

fn3.rationale: Two sentences give a result, two give a reason, one shows something different and one gives the time. The word in bold tells you which job comes next.

itens: The client did not answer, {so|90px} I called again.
We could not start the meeting {because|120px} the projector was not working.
The flight was late {because of|130px} the weather.
The report is ready, {but|90px} the numbers from June are missing.
Ryan will tell the team {when|90px} he gets the new laptop.

abertura: A quick reference to the situation and the language you used.
